comparisons.reviewed_wording: In an interim order dated 4 June 2026, the Tribunal judiciaire de Caen ordered Carrefour France to provide e-commerce services complying with French accessibility requirements. A €500 daily penalty applies if non-compliance continues six months after the order. The court also ordered Carrefour to pay a total of €10,000 in provisional damages to apiDV and Droit Pluriel, the costs of the proceedings, and €3,000 under article 700 of the French Code of Civil Procedure.
comparisons.source_summary: See matching claim passage and reference in country research; full original-language reviewer packet was supplied independently.

comparisons.reviewed_wording: On 24 March 2026, the Netherlands Authority for Consumers and Markets (ACM) reported tests of approximately 100 of the largest Dutch online stores, as well as websites operated by large telecom and energy providers. In its 24 March 2026 report, ACM said it would contact the largest companies with the poorest results. Companies contacted by ACM that failed to make sufficient improvements would risk enforcement action.

comparisons.reviewed_wording: Products: On 23 October 2025, Sweden’s Post and Telecom Authority (PTS) announced checks of laptops, smartphones and tablets, focusing on EU declarations of conformity and certain digital product information.

comparisons.reviewed_wording: E-commerce: On 15 October 2025, PTS announced that its first checks of e-commerce services had begun. This round covered the websites of larger operators established in Sweden that sell products online. The checks focused on the homepage, a product page and search; apps were excluded.

comparisons.reviewed_wording: Banking: On 8 September 2026, PTS announced that checks of banking services had begun, targeting larger operators established in Sweden. The checks would start with these operators’ reports of shortcomings. Work was planned for 2026–2027.

The countries were given two months to respond and take the necessary measures.

comparisons.reviewed_wording: Type: Government agency — other accessibility law. Status: Closed. Norway’s ICT accessibility authority (Uu-tilsynet) closed its case concerning Helseplattformen AS’s HelsaMi website on 23 December 2025 after the remaining identified errors were corrected. Daily penalties of NOK 50,000 began on 20 December; the authority reports that the penalties applied for two days. The case concerned Norway’s Equality and Anti-Discrimination Act and ICT accessibility regulation.
